clue.text: Piped music originally played in tower

indicators.note: originally asks for the opening letter of each of the two words that follow it

parts.note: a broch is a round prehistoric stone tower found in Scotland

explanation.surface: Bagpipe music was first heard echoing inside a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the first letters of 'played' and 'in', giving PI; a BROCH is an Iron Age drystone tower of northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A pibroch is a classical bagpipe composition, so it is music produced by pipes.

clue.text: Assumes it's restricted by lawmen out East

indicators.note: restricted by means held within the lawmen's word
out means the compass letter is removed

parts.note: a posse is a band of men summoned by a sheriff to enforce the law
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone supposes the sheriff's men have it cornered with the East cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: A posse is a sheriff's band of deputies in the American West; the 's of 'it's' is just 'is', part of the passive 'is restricted'.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward as a basis for argument, i.e. to assume.

clue.text: Like an uncouth person expecting a fall in prices?

definitions.meaning: gruff and rough-mannered, like a grizzly
in stock-market slang a bear sells in anticipation of falling prices

explanation.surface: A boorish investor gloomily predicts a market drop.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear in finance anticipates decline, and a rude oaf is likened to the animal.

clue.text: Unfashionable garments in the suburbs

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
skirts are garments

explanation.surface: Dated clothing is worn on the edge of town.
explanation.definitionFit: The outskirts are the outer parts of a town, its suburban fringe.

clue.text: Hard to see plant that is with another that's wild

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
the arum is a plant, the lily family's cuckoo-pint
sc, short for Latin scilicet, means namely or that is
another of the same plant, so the arum again

explanation.surface: A botanist finds one plant hard to spot alongside a wild one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to see' is a link; SC (scilicet) is the scholarly abbreviation for 'that is to say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Harum-scarum describes reckless, unruly behaviour, so it means wild.

clue.text: Fluster rarely, being so relaxed

indicators.note: rarely in the sense of unusually or exceptionally signals the letters of the previous word rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who seldom gets in a flap must be calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rarely' is the anagram signal on FLUSTER; 'being so' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restful is calm and soothing, a synonym of relaxed in the sense of free from tension.

clue.text: Perch used by an angler

definitions.meaning: an old unit of length of five and a half yards, also called a pole
the fishing pole an angler casts with

explanation.definitionFit: A rod is both a measure of length equal to a perch and the angler's fishing pole.

clue.text: Some of this is a likely constituent of rope

indicators.note: some of means only part of the following words is taken, a run of consecutive letters

explanation.surface: Part of this material will probably go into a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some of' points to the letters spanning thiS IS A Likely.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a strong plant fibre from an agave, used to make cord and rope.

clue.text: Alarm about source of explosive found in cargo

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the alarm wraps round the next letter

parts.note: fright is alarm or sudden fear

indicators.note: source of takes the first letter of explosive

explanation.surface: Panic as a bomb is discovered among goods being shipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is a link; E goes inside FRIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is goods carried by ship, train or lorry, i.e. cargo.

clue.text: Cosmetic for colouring cheek and stomach?

parts.note: lip means cheek or insolence, as in 'none of your lip'
to stomach is to stick, put up with

explanation.surface: A product to add colour to the face and belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheek' and 'stomach' look like body parts but are verbs and slang: impudence and tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinted waxy stick applied to the mouth is a cosmetic that colours it.

clue.text: Broadcast featuring animal in desert storm

indicators.note: in places the animal inside the stormed letters
storm suggests turmoil, telling us to churn the letters of the word desert

parts.note: a cat is a common animal

explanation.surface: A news report shows a creature caught in a sandstorm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' rearranges the desert to STERED; 'featuring' is only a link, and 'Broadcast' is the past participle of sowing widely.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed that is broadcast is sown by flinging it widely, so it ends up strewn about.

clue.text: It's a lottery, this sortie by aircraft

definitions.meaning: short for sweepstake, a lottery in which the stakes go to the winners
a ... flight across an area by military planes

explanation.definitionFit: A sweepstake is a lottery, often shortened; and a sweep is also a planes' offensive pass over territory.

clue.text: The knack of getting runs in a very short time

indicators.note: in tells us the runs abbreviation sits inside the short time

parts.note: a tick is an instant, as in 'back in a tick'
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A batsman's skill in scoring quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket scoring R stands for runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A trick is a clever way of doing something, a synonym of knack or skill.

clue.text: Reflected glow finally seen in low fire

indicators.note: in places that final letter between the other pieces

parts.note: to low is to make the sound a cow makes, moo
to fire something is to light it

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word seen that follows it

explanation.surface: A faint glow is at last visible in a dying fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the cow's verb, not the opposite of high; the N sits between the two synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon has no light of its own, so its glow is sunlight bounced back off it.

clue.text: Exploit unreasonably, having finished prison sentence

parts.note: over means ended, finished
a stretch is slang for a term in prison

explanation.surface: A released convict is pushed too hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstretch something is to strain or use it beyond its sensible limits.

clue.text: Typical pose by daily given to controversy

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British cleaning woman who comes in each day
to pose is to put on an act
eristic describes someone fond of argument and dispute

explanation.surface: A cleaner predictably adopts a stance on any argument.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' or CHAR is British slang for a charwoman, a hired house cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Something characteristic is distinctive of a person or kind, hence typical.

clue.text: In island location, king put up old Jew

indicators.note: in means the king is placed inside the word for location

parts.note: a site is a location

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means written upwards, so the king's name is reversed

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A monarch is raised up in an island settlement of ancient Hebrews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' in a down clue reverses the king to RAEL, which slots after the first letter of the location; King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Israelites were the ancient Hebrew people, descendants of Jacob, so biblical Jews.

clue.text: Cold 'drink' served on carriage? Nonsense!

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
to lap is to drink as a cat does
a trap is a light two-wheeled horse carriage

explanation.surface: A cold drink is offered on a coach journey, and someone objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink' is in quotes because to lap is how an animal drinks; 'served on' puts it on top of TRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious or empty talk, meaning nonsense.

clue.text: Coin once given by member to powerful jazzman

parts.note: the louis was a gold coin of pre-revolutionary France
an arm is a limb, or member, of the body
strong means powerful

explanation.surface: A collector hands an old coin to a forceful musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Satchmo was the famous New Orleans trumpeter and singer, a jazz musician.

clue.text: Part of one's goal, being honourable

definitions.meaning: a goalpost, one of the vertical posts of a goal

explanation.definitionFit: A goal's vertical post is called this, and the word also means principled.

clue.text: So, for example, permitted a brief communication

parts.note: so (soh) is an example of a musical note in the sol-fa scale
let means permitted

explanation.surface: Thus, for instance, a short message was allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So' is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale, more often spelt soh, not 'therefore'.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded card for a short letter, i.e. a brief message.

clue.text: Crackpot plan to capture a military assistant

indicators.note: capture means hold within, so the plan wraps the assistant

parts.note: a map or plan of a place
ADC is aide-de-camp, an officer assisting a general

explanation.surface: A lunatic scheme to seize an officer's aide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is just a link; aide-de-camp is the officer who serves as a general's personal assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap is a recklessly impulsive person, close in sense to a crackpot.

clue.text: Agent thrown over by one-time artiste

indicators.note: thrown over means flipped round, so the agent's word is read backwards

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is an agent
one-time means former, previous

explanation.surface: A has-been entertainer is dumped by their agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown over' turns REP into PER; 'by' just sets it beside FORMER.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer, someone who gives shows.

clue.text: Greybeard's endless portrayal of a military man

indicators.note: endless means both outer letters of the military word are dropped

parts.note: a soldier is a military man

explanation.surface: An old man is endlessly depicted as a fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes the first and last letters off SOLDIER; 'portrayal of a' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is informal for an elderly person, as a greybeard is.

clue.text: Additional skill displayed in retirement by former partner

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or lover

indicators.note: retirement means withdrawing or going back, so the word for skill is shown backwards

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: An ex-spouse shows off an extra talent after retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed in retirement' gives TRA, the skill word read backwards, placed after the former partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, more than is usual or expected.

clue.text: Saintly woman beheaded for being inflexible

indicators.note: beheaded means the head, or first letter, of the saint's name is cut off

parts.note: St Brigid is a patron saint of Ireland

explanation.surface: A female saint is executed for refusing to bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' drops the first letter of BRIGID, Ireland's female patron saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means stiff and unbending, a synonym of inflexible.

clue.text: Very bitter civil disturbance involving music group

indicators.note: involving means taking the music group inside
disturbance means the letters of civil are disordered

parts.note: a trio is a group of three musicians

explanation.surface: A bitter riot erupts, starring a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbance' rearranges the civil letters to VILIC, and 'involving' wraps them round the group after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriolic speech is caustic and savage, like sulphuric acid, hence harshly bitter.

clue.text: Charge initially levied for a large vessel

definitions.meaning: Value Added Tax, a charge known by its initials and levied on sales
a big tub or tank for liquids, as in brewing

explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' hints that the tax is named by its initials, V A T, a British sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Value Added Tax is a British sales tax, and a brewer's tank for liquid has the same name.

clue.text: Sick person clearly in evidence around one

indicators.note: around means the evident word wraps round the numeral

parts.note: patent means obvious, plainly visible
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An invalid is obviously walking round.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient is someone receiving medical care, an invalid under treatment.

clue.text: The pale concoction that's at the bottom of the glass

definitions.text: that's at the bottom of the glass

indicators.note: a concoction is something mixed up, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A pale drink leaves dregs in the tumbler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' rearranges the letters of THE PALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A heeltap is the small amount of liquor left in a drinking vessel after drinking.
